title: McDonald's Deploys Archy AI Drive-Thru to Combat Competition
summary: McDonald's rolls out Archy, an AI order-taker, across US drive-thrus by end of 2027. The system takes 90% of orders accurately and frees up 50 hours weekly.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- McDonald's is deploying Archy AI drive-thru ordering across US locations, achieving 90% accuracy and freeing 50 hours of labor weekly per restaurant.
- The $800,000 per-store Next remodel includes hand-breaded chicken prep, premium beverages, and open kitchens to compete with Raising Cane's and 7 Brew.
- Franchisees resist the multibillion-dollar overhaul amid weak traffic, with McDonald's promising payback in four years and $100,000 extra annual cash flow.


McDonald's has officially launched Archy, an artificial intelligence-powered drive-thru ordering system, in Chicago-area test markets as part of a sweeping $19 billion restaurant overhaul. The deployment marks a critical component of CEO Chris Kempczinski's strategy to modernize the chain's operations while fending off competition from upstart rivals like Raising Cane's and 7 Brew. Archy takes approximately 90% of orders accurately and is expected to free up 50 hours of labor each week per location, addressing both efficiency and service quality challenges that have plagued the brand.


## Archy AI System Performance and Rollout Timeline


Officially launched on November 24, 2026, the Archy AI system has been conducting live tests in Chicago-area McDonald's locations throughout the year. During October 2026 evaluations, the system responded in approximately three seconds after customers finished speaking in English, a significant improvement from the eight-second lag observed in June 2026. The AI correctly processed orders including complex meal customizations like medium Deluxe McCrispy meals with Diet Coke and Quarter Pounders without cheese, though it occasionally stumbled over pronunciation of menu items.


Spanish-language interactions showed longer response times of around eight seconds, with the system displaying an inconsistent accent that sometimes sounded non-native. While Archy captured the order correctly, confirmation boards displayed the information in English rather than Spanish. McDonald's expects the technology to reach a majority of US restaurants by the end of 2027, with franchisees having already invested at least $35,000 per store on upgraded servers and supporting infrastructure.


## The Next Remodel Strategy and Franchisee Resistance


The Archy deployment operates within McDonald's broader Next remodel initiative, which requires franchisees to spend $800,000 per location on comprehensive upgrades. These changes include removing kitchen walls installed less than a decade ago, adding hand-breaded chicken preparation stations with stainless steel counters and deep batter pans, and expanding cafe stations for premium beverages made with Red Bull and freeze-dried dragon fruit. The company has committed $8.5 billion to support franchisees across approximately 24,000 US and select international locations over the next 10 years.


Franchisee pushback has been substantial. More than 50% of locations opened in 2026 are projected to fall below sales targets by 10% or more in their first year, continuing a deteriorating trend from 34% in 2023 and 13% in 2022. Operators argue that weak traffic, elevated costs, and existing debt from the previous $6 billion Experience of the Future remodel completed between 2018 and 2020 leave little financial bandwidth. McDonald's US President Skye Anderson acknowledged in October 2026 that the plan is weighing heavy on operators' minds and confirmed no commitment letters would be required before year-end 2026.


## Hand-Breaded Chicken and Premium Menu Expansion


The Next remodel centers on hand-breaded chicken as McDonald's boldest bet to grow its $30 billion chicken business. Whole-muscle chicken arrives marinated, raw, and frozen, then gets thawed in refrigerated cabinets before workers dip it in batter pans and bread it by hand. The labor-intensive process produces crunchier, juicier results than frozen nuggets but raises cross-contamination concerns that McDonald's is addressing through revised workflows. The chain already operates hand-breaded chicken in 10,000 Asian locations and plans to expand US testing from a handful of Chicago stores to 100 restaurants in early 2027.


Premium beverages including Strawberry Watermelon Refreshers and Red Bull Dragonberry Energizers drive orders 50% larger than average and boost sales after lunch hours. At Chicago test locations, a Deluxe McCrispy Chicken Sandwich costs $5.99 and four strips run $6.39, compared to $1.99 for a smaller frozen McChicken. This pricing strategy aims to balance affordability with quality, though only 20% of diners currently give McDonald's high marks on value according to Technomic research, trailing fast-food industry averages.


## Competitive Pressure from Raising Cane's and 7 Brew


McDonald's modernization push directly responds to market share losses to focused competitors. Raising Cane's earns top food quality marks from nearly two-thirds of diners, compared to just 36% for McDonald's, according to Technomic surveys. The chicken finger specialist's cooked-to-order model and secret dipping sauce have created long customer lines, while 7 Brew's bubbly baristas serving colorful sweet drinks have captured the beverage-focused quick-service segment. McDonald's ranks at or near the bottom among major chains on food quality, friendly service, and atmosphere metrics.


The company's US same-store sales have slumped as Americans trim fast-food spending amid elevated gas prices, housing costs, and grocery bills. Investors have knocked $22.6 billion off McDonald's market value in 2026, reflecting skepticism about the turnaround strategy. Deutsche Bank Securities estimates that fully rolling out Next across all targeted locations could cost upward of $19 billion, far exceeding McDonald's $8.5 billion commitment and requiring franchisees to shoulder substantial expense.


## What This Means for Fast-Food Automation


McDonald's Archy deployment represents the most aggressive AI automation push by a major fast-food chain, with roughly two-thirds of the company's US sales flowing through drive-thru lanes. The system's 90% accuracy rate and 50-hour weekly labor savings could reshape industry economics if McDonald's can prove a four-year payback period and $100,000 annual cash flow increases for franchisees. However, the broader Next remodel's success hinges on whether premium hand-breaded chicken and elevated beverages can attract quality-focused customers without alienating McDonald's value-seeking core base. Franchisee negotiations continuing into early 2027 will determine if the company can balance affordability with premiumization, or if the strategy spreads resources too thin across competing customer priorities.
